observations: Firefox and WebKit under emulated forced colors draw the disabled native checked box light: Firefox uses fill rgb(199,199,206) with a white tick on white, the same in light and dark (dispatch://INFRA-527/artifact/tester-r2-firefox-light-active-png). It is visibly filled against an empty outline, but below the spec's 128-per-channel bar, so the forced-colors rows read 0 strong pixels in those engines (not in CI's matrix for this spec). Chromium's emulation uses the Windows High Contrast palettes and passes. [inference] Real Firefox on Windows High Contrast uses the theme's GrayText, which those palettes make high contrast, and real Safari has no forced-colors mode; WCAG 1.4.11 exempts inactive (disabled) components. Not recorded as a failure.

expectBoxesLookDifferent compares two element screenshots taken at different positions. In the run with the forced-colors block deleted, the chromium-dark row passed once in 4 runs although both boxes were drawn alike. The other three forced-colors rows caught the regression in every run, so the lock holds, but that one row's oracle is not deterministic on a broken build.
Round-1 notes stand: the inline variant and MarkdownPreview draw no box (plan D5), and the implementer's open question on the collapsed preview is with the INFRA-138 architect.
